reconciliation.note: crawl_run_findings holds 18 rows (one per rule, with a count column); crawl_run_finding_instances holds 7,298 (one per occurrence). findings_cmd serves the 7,298 instances. Every per-rule number in this report is an INSTANCE count. At rule level the run found 18 issues, not 7,298.

defects.observed: 3,830 anchor-missing findings on this page, presented as a complete count
defects.expected: 11,113 anchors without an accessible name (5,652 of them .xml links). The crawler stored bodyTruncated=true and decodedSize=5,000,000 against a real body of 14,383,618 bytes, so it parsed the first 5MB and counted what it saw. Confirmed by fetching the page independently and counting anchors with cheerio.
defects.repro: evidence/anchor-missing__1.http — load, count $('a') with no text/aria-label/title/img[alt]

defects.observed: 966 of 1,021 findings report detail 'Timed out' for two icann.org footer links (483 each)
defects.expected: HTTP 301, served promptly. The link is not broken. The crawl requested icann.org 483+ times for the same two URLs, so the timeout is most likely self-inflicted rather than a property of the destination.

Exactly one document <title> ('Performance'). The other 48 are <title> elements inside inline <svg>, which are SVG accessibility labels carrying chart data ('August 2025: 100%'), not document titles. Same on /dnssec/tcrs with 41.

defects.observed: 484 separate page-scoped findings, each with detail:'' and detectedValue:''. Accounts for 484 of the run's 486 total errors.
defects.expected: The underlying condition is real — robots.txt declares no Sitemap and /sitemap.xml returns 404, so the site publishes none. But it is one site-level fact, and emitting it 484 times with no evidence payload makes the error count a single condition counted 484 times.
Detection is correct — the page genuinely has no meta description. But an issue record with no observed value gives a developer nothing to locate.

defects.observed: 483 findings for one footer link to icann.org, scope=template
defects.expected: Classification and wording are correct (403 proves refusal, not absence) and the target really does return 403 behind Cloudflare. But scope=template is already known, so one finding with a page count would say the same thing 483 times more usefully.
